images.title: 기본 공간과 조작
images.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Make one 16:10 image of a PRACTICAL implementable Depth AI interaction design, styled as a straightforward realtime Unity prototype viewport. This is an interface reference, NOT a product advertisement or a photograph. The previous design was rejected for expensive shiny decorative renderings and unclear actual usability.

Visual specification: neutral cool light-gray background, simple ground-plane grid with perspective, ONE soft directional light. Basic opaque pale blue / light gray cubes made of six flat square faces, hard or minimally beveled edges, flat diffuse shading, black-gray thin visible edges. Truly equal width/height/depth. No glass, no glossy reflections, no bloom/glow, no blurred room, no architecture, no depth of field, no metal sockets, no thick physical cables, no decorative icons. Looks feasible with stock Unity cube primitives, a ground grid, thin LineRenderer connections and text labels. All text crisp and modest, not giant advertising typography.

Composition: the 3D viewport fills almost the entire frame. Only a thin modest top toolbar says "DEPTH AI / Checkout" and "Select   Rotate   Orbit   Reset". Small blue hollow cube logo. Small bottom hint says "Click: open contents | Drag empty space: orbit | Wheel: zoom". Small "Interaction mockup" bottom right. This is the proposed spatial app view, no Unity editor hierarchy, no docked desktop dashboard.

At left is a small upright source-linked Checkout preview plane, about 20% width, simple neutral UI reading "Checkout preview", "Mug 48", "Plant 72", "Subtotal 120", "Discount 20%", "Total 96", "Apply coupon". It remains a secondary view.
Six medium-small actual solid cube CONTAINERS occupy distinct positions in the remaining 3D space with generous gaps. Front center: CheckoutController. To its right CartState. Higher and behind CouponRules. Far right CouponValidator. Lower right TotalsView. Back-left CartSummary. Each container body is simple and functional. Use small separate camera-facing fixed-size white label strips just ABOVE cubes, names plus member counts: CheckoutController / 4 members; CartState / 5 members; CouponRules / 2 members; CouponValidator / 1 member; TotalsView / 1 member; CartSummary / 1 member. Only these six cubes, no extra objects. Labels are crisp, never printed skewed across cube faces. Perspective size and grid show depth without making distant labels tiny.

Tiny flat circle port markers directly on cube faces (just colored disks, no mechanical plugs). Show ONLY TWO thin blue source-relationship lines: CheckoutController to CouponRules and CheckoutController to CouponValidator, each from face marker to face marker. These are container-aggregated call relationships. No other cables. One cube CartState has a thin blue selected outline with a small nearby action "Open 5 members". No particle effects, rotation halos or elaborate animations. The screenshot should tell a developer exactly what simple geometry and controls to build and tell a user what they can click. Practical everyday tool, moderately polished, restrained, tangible real 3D cubes.
images.description: 컨테이너 큐브와 연결을 탐색합니다. 작은 미리보기는 공간 왼쪽에 유지하고, 각 큐브에는 이름과 내부 모듈 수를 표시합니다.
